headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure improvements, particularly those driven by high energy users like data centers, away from residential ratepayers and onto those large users.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia energy plan targets utility costs, data center growth
news_summary: Virginia's new energy plan proposes requiring utilities to share fuel costs and making data centers pay for the electricity infrastructure costs they create. The plan aims to address rising power demand and ensure costs are appropriately assigned rather than shifted to households and small businesses.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water providers to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers, increasing transparency and providing data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, community groups, transparency advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (due to compliance burden).
news_headline: SB553: Data center water use reporting signed into law
news_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers, addressing concerns about dwindling groundwater resources. The bill, which passed both chambers and was signed into law, provides the Virginia DEQ with better information for water resource management.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise studies, and allows localities to require information on environmental impacts, giving communities more control over data center development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community groups, residential advocates, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to increased regulatory burden and potential restrictions).
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: Virginia has enacted a new law, HB 153, which requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments, including noise studies, and disclose utility infrastructure. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local officials.
